question: Which among the following international boundaries is the longest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo-Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India shares its land border with seven neighbouring countries — the Indo-Bangladesh border is the longest, at approximately 4,096 km, running through West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. (भारत-बांग्लादेश सीमा — सबसे लंबी सीमा)

 

• This border is guarded by the Border Security Force (BSF) and parts of it were demarcated by the Radcliffe Line in 1947.

 

• The next-longest borders are the Indo-China border (~3,488 km, largely along the disputed McMahon Line) and the Indo-Pakistan border (~3,323 km).

 

• The Indo-Myanmar border (~1,643 km) is comparatively short and passes through Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's total land border length is about 15,106.7 km, shared with Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan.

 

• The Indo-Nepal border (~1,751 km) is largely open, and citizens of both countries can cross freely under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship.

 

NOTE

 

• Indo-Myanmar (Option 2): At around 1,643 km, this is one of the shorter Indian international borders.

 

• Indo-China (Option 3): The second-longest border (~3,488 km), largely following the disputed McMahon Line.

 

• Indo-Pak (Option 4): About 3,323 km long, demarcated mostly by the Radcliffe Line and the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir.

question: Who was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalpana Chawla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalpana Chawla, born in Karnal, Haryana, was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space, flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-87) in 1997 as a mission specialist. (कल्पना चावला — भारतीय मूल की प्रथम महिला अंतरिक्ष यात्री)

 

• She flew a second mission in 2003 on STS-107, and tragically died when the Columbia shuttle disintegrated during re-entry on 1 February 2003.

 

• She was posthumously awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor by the United States government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sunita Williams, another astronaut of Indian origin, holds records for spacewalks by a woman and has flown multiple long-duration missions to the ISS.

 

• Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian citizen to go to space, flying aboard Soyuz T-11 in 1984.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagin Cox (Option 1): An Indian-American aerospace engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, known for her work on Mars missions — not an astronaut.

 

• Yogita Shah (Option 2): Not a known astronaut; a distractor option.

 

• Sirisha Bandla (Option 4): An Indian-American aerospace engineer who flew to space in July 2021 aboard Virgin Galactic's VSS Unity on a suborbital flight — after Kalpana Chawla.

question: Under which article of the Indian constitution is the Prime Minister the head of the Council of Ministers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 74.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President in the exercise of their functions. (अनुच्छेद 74 — मंत्रिपरिषद)

 

• This provision is part of Part V of the Constitution, which deals with the Union executive.

 

• Following the 42nd and 44th Constitutional Amendments, the President is bound to act in accordance with the aid and advice tendered by the Council of Ministers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 75 deals with the appointment, term, and other conditions of service of ministers.

 

• Article 78 lays down the duties of the Prime Minister with respect to furnishing information to the President.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 52 (Option 1): Provides for the office of the President of India ("There shall be a President of India").

 

• Article 377 (Option 2): Not a provision of the Constitution related to the Council of Ministers; it echoes the number of the (now-read-down) Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code and is a distractor here.

 

• Article 60 (Option 3): Prescribes the oath or affirmation to be made by the President before entering office.

question: The Indian parliament has power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse through which article of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 302.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 302 empowers Parliament to impose, by law, such restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse between one State and another, or within any part of India's territory, as may be required in the public interest.

 

• This provision falls under Part XIII (Articles 301–307) of the Constitution, which governs trade, commerce and intercourse within India. (भाग XIII — व्यापार, वाणिज्य और व्यवहार)

 

• Article 301 lays down the general rule of freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India, and Article 302 is the exception that lets Parliament restrict it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 303 restricts the power of both Parliament and State Legislatures to make discriminatory trade laws, except in cases of scarcity.

 

• Article 304 empowers a State Legislature (not Parliament) to impose reasonable restrictions on trade with other States, subject to the President's prior sanction.

 

NOTE

 

• 304 (Option 1): Empowers a State Legislature, not Parliament, to restrict trade with other states in the public interest.

 

• 300A (Option 2): States that no person shall be deprived of their property save by authority of law (Right to Property) — unrelated to trade restrictions.

 

• 303 (Option 3): Restricts Parliament's and States' power to make laws giving preference to one state over another in trade and commerce matters.

question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum – Annelida?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Earthworm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The earthworm (e.g., *Pheretima*, *Lumbricus*) belongs to Phylum Annelida, characterised by a segmented (metameric) body with a true coelom. (केंचुआ — संघ एनेलिडा)

 

• Annelids possess a closed circulatory system and a nervous system built around a ventral nerve cord.

 

• Other classic annelid examples include leeches (*Hirudinaria*) and marine bristle worms such as *Nereis* (a polychaete).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phylum Annelida is divided into three classes: Polychaeta (mostly marine, e.g., Nereis), Oligochaeta (e.g., earthworm), and Hirudinea (leeches).

 

• Charles Darwin studied earthworms extensively for their role in soil formation and aeration.

 

NOTE

 

• Hookworm (Option 1): Belongs to Phylum Nematoda (*Ancylostoma duodenale*), a parasitic roundworm.

 

• Filaria worm (Option 2): Also belongs to Phylum Nematoda (*Wuchereria bancrofti* causes filariasis).

 

• Roundworm (Option 4): The common roundworm (*Ascaris*) is itself the type organism of Phylum Nematoda, not Annelida.

question: Which among the following enzymes helps in breaking down fats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lipase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lipase is the enzyme that breaks down (hydrolyses) fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol. (लाइपेज — वसा को तोड़ने वाला एंजाइम)

 

• It is secreted mainly by the pancreas, and is also present in gastric juice and the small intestine.

 

• Bile, produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, emulsifies fats to increase their surface area for digestion, but it is not itself an enzyme — lipase carries out the actual chemical breakdown.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pancreatic juice contains a full complement of digestive enzymes, including lipase, amylase, and trypsinogen (activated to trypsin).

 

• In humans, most fat digestion occurs in the small intestine, aided by bile emulsification and pancreatic lipase.

 

NOTE

 

• Amylase (Option 2): Breaks down starch and other carbohydrates into simpler sugars such as maltose.

 

• Trypsin (Option 3): A proteolytic enzyme that breaks down proteins into peptides and amino acids.

 

• Ribonuclease (Option 4): Breaks down RNA into smaller components; it acts on nucleic acids, not fats.

question: Cheetahs brought from Namibia were introduced in the Kuno National Park located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuno National Park is located in the Sheopur and Morena districts of Madhya Pradesh. (कुनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Under “Project Cheetah,” cheetahs brought from Namibia were released into Kuno National Park in September 2022, reintroducing the species to India after it had gone extinct in the country in 1952.

 

• A second batch of cheetahs was later brought from South Africa in February 2023 as part of the same reintroduction effort.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kuno National Park was originally developed and notified as a wildlife sanctuary that had also been proposed decades earlier as a second home for Asiatic lions from Gir, Gujarat — a relocation that has not yet materialised.

 

• The cheetah reintroduction is guided by the “Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India.”

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Home to protected areas like Bandipur and Nagarhole, but not Kuno National Park.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Home to Gir National Park, the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion, not Kuno.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Home to Ranthambore and Sariska tiger reserves, not Kuno National Park.

question: Which among the following is an Indian martial art from Manipur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thang-Ta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thang-Ta (also called Huyen Lallong) is a traditional martial art from Manipur, involving the use of the sword (*thang*) and spear (*ta*). (थांग-ता — मणिपुर की मार्शल आर्ट)

 

• It combines armed combat with unarmed combat techniques (*Sarit Sarak*) and carries deep spiritual and ritual significance in Manipuri culture.

 

• Manipur is also known for other traditional sports such as Mukna (wrestling) and Sagol Kangjei (a form of polo believed to have originated there).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Indian martial arts include Kalaripayattu (Kerala), Gatka (Punjab), Silambam (Tamil Nadu), and Mardani Khel (Maharashtra).

 

NOTE

 

• Muay Thai (Option 1): A striking martial art that originated in Thailand, not India.

 

• Kalaripayattu (Option 2): One of the oldest martial arts in the world, originating in Kerala.

 

• Gatka (Option 4): A Sikh martial art from Punjab involving swords and sticks.

question: ______ will host the 37th edition of the National Games in October 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Goa was confirmed to host, and did host, the 37th National Games of India, held in October–November 2023. (गोवा — 37वें राष्ट्रीय खेलों का मेजबान)

 

• It featured a record number of sporting disciplines (43 disciplines) and was the first time Goa hosted the National Games.

 

• The Games had originally been scheduled earlier but were postponed multiple times, including because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 36th National Games were held in Gujarat in 2022.

 

• The National Games of India are organised by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and are usually held once every two years.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Was not the host of the 37th National Games.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Has hosted National Games in the past, but not the 37th edition.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Has hosted National Games in the past (e.g., 1994), but not the 37th edition.

question: Who is the governor of Reserve Bank of India as of 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shaktikanta Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shaktikanta Das, a former IAS officer (1980 batch), has served as the 25th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India since December 2018, and continued to hold this post through 2022 after being reappointed for a second term in December 2021. (शक्तिकांत दास — RBI गवर्नर)

 

• Before becoming RBI Governor, he served as India's Economic Affairs Secretary and Revenue Secretary.

 

• He succeeded Urjit R. Patel, who resigned as Governor in December 2018.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and is headquartered in Mumbai.

 

• Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI, while C.D. Deshmukh was its first Indian Governor.

 

NOTE

 

• Urjit R. Patel (Option 1): Served as RBI Governor from 2016 to December 2018, immediately before Das.

 

• D. Subbarao (Option 2): Served as RBI Governor from 2008 to 2013.

 

• Raghuram Rajan (Option 4): Served as RBI Governor from 2013 to 2016.

question: Nechiphu Tunnel, in Arunachal Pradesh, built by Border Road Organisation (BRO) and its excavation work completed in May 2022 falls under Project ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vartak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nechiphu Tunnel in Arunachal Pradesh, built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), falls under Project Vartak, which handles road construction along the strategically important Balipara–Chariduar–Tawang axis. (प्रोजेक्ट वर्तक — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Its excavation work was completed in May 2022; the tunnel bypasses the landslide-prone Nechiphu Pass Y-junction on the route to Tawang.

 

• The tunnel significantly improves all-weather connectivity for troops and civilians heading to forward areas near the China border.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• BRO operates numerous named projects across border states — for example, Project Dantak in Bhutan, Project Beacon in Himachal Pradesh/Ladakh, and Project Swastik in Sikkim.

 

NOTE

 

• Hirak (Option 1): A BRO project responsible for road construction in Manipur.

 

• Sampark (Option 2): A BRO project responsible for road construction in Mizoram.

 

• Gaganyaan (Option 3): India's first crewed spaceflight programme run by ISRO, unrelated to BRO's road-building projects.

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan, an Indian musician credited with popularizing the shehnai, received which honour from Government of India in 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Ratna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan, the legendary shehnai maestro, was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2001. (भारत रत्न — उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान)

 

• He is credited with popularising the shehnai as a solo classical concert instrument, and famously performed at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day (15 August 1947) and on Republic Day 1950.

 

• Before the Bharat Ratna, he had already received the Padma Shri (1961), Padma Bhushan (1968), and Padma Vibhushan (1980) — one of the few artists to receive all these honours in sequence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan was born in Dumraon, Bihar, and spent most of his career in Varanasi, closely associated with the Kashi Vishwanath Temple.

 

• He is one of only a handful of classical musicians — along with M.S. Subbulakshmi, Bhimsen Joshi, and Ravi Shankar — to have received the Bharat Ratna.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri (Option 2): India's fourth-highest civilian award, which Khan received earlier, in 1961.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 3): India's second-highest civilian award, received by Khan in 1980.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 4): India's third-highest civilian award, received by Khan in 1968.

question: The commercial banks of India have to maintain a minimum percentage of cash, gold and other securities before lending loans to its customers. This is called the ______.
option_2: Current Account and Savings Account Ratio
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statutory Liquidity Ratio.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the minimum percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that it must maintain in the form of cash, gold, and other approved (unencumbered) securities before extending loans to customers. (सांविधिक तरलता अनुपात — SLR)

 

• SLR is maintained by the bank itself (unlike CRR, which is deposited with the RBI), and is regulated under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

 

• It is one of the monetary tools the RBI uses to control liquidity, inflation, and credit growth in the economy, while also ensuring bank solvency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• SLR can range from 0% to 40% of NDTL as per RBI's discretion; it stood at 18% around 2022.

 

• SLR and CRR together form key quantitative monetary policy instruments, alongside the repo rate and reverse repo rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Capital Adequacy Ratio (Option 1): Measures a bank's capital relative to its risk-weighted assets to ensure solvency — unrelated to holding cash/gold reserves before lending.

 

• Current Account and Savings Account Ratio (Option 2): The proportion of low-cost CASA deposits to a bank's total deposits, indicating cost of funds — not a statutory reserve requirement.

 

• Cash Reserve Ratio (Option 4): The minimum percentage of NDTL a bank must keep purely as cash with the RBI — it does not include gold or securities, and is not held by the bank itself.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "river – tributary" is correct?
I. Tapi – Manjra
II. Krishna – Ghatprabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: The Manjra (Manjira) River is a tributary of the Godavari River, not the Tapi. It originates in the Balaghat Range and joins the Godavari in Nizamabad district, Telangana.

 

• Statement II is correct: The Ghatprabha (Ghataprabha) River is a tributary of the Krishna River. It originates in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra and joins the Krishna near Kudalasangama in Karnataka. (घटप्रभा — कृष्णा नदी की सहायक नदी)

 

• The Tapi River's actual major tributaries include the Purna, Girna, Panzara, and Waghur rivers, not the Manjra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Krishna River, India's fourth-longest river, has other major tributaries including the Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, and Musi.

 

• The Godavari River, the second-longest river in India, is often called the “Dakshin Ganga.”

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, since statement II (Krishna–Ghatprabha) is a valid pairing.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, since the Manjra is a tributary of the Godavari, not the Tapi.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect, since statement I is a wrong pairing.

question: Which of the following is not a technique or a step to convert normal water to potable water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bromination.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bromination (adding bromine) is primarily used as a disinfectant for swimming pools and spas, not as a standard step in converting ordinary water into potable (drinking) water.

 

• Standard techniques used to make water potable include filtration (removing suspended particles), boiling (killing pathogens), and chlorination (disinfecting with chlorine, the most common method for municipal water supply). (क्लोरीनीकरण — पेयजल शुद्धिकरण)

 

• Other common potabilisation steps include coagulation-flocculation, sedimentation, and disinfection using UV light or ozone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorination is the most widely used, cost-effective method for large-scale disinfection of municipal drinking water supplies.

 

• Reverse osmosis (RO) and activated-carbon filters are common household-level water purification technologies.

 

NOTE

 

• Filtration (Option 1): A genuine, standard technique used to remove suspended impurities from water.

 

• Boiling (Option 3): A traditional and effective method for killing disease-causing microorganisms in water.

 

• Chlorination (Option 4): The standard chemical disinfection method used by municipal water treatment plants.

question: In a completely connected network, how many lines are required for connecting 6 nodes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a completely connected network (graph) with n nodes, the number of connecting lines (edges) required is given by the formula: n(n − 1)/2.

 

• For n = 6: Number of lines = 6 × 5 / 2 = 15.

 

• This is because each node connects to every other node exactly once, and dividing by 2 avoids counting each connection twice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This formula is equivalent to the combination formula ⁿC₂, representing the number of ways to choose 2 nodes out of n to form a connection.

 

• A fully connected (complete) network with n nodes is denoted Kₙ in graph theory.

 

NOTE

 

• 12 (Option 1): Not the correct value; would result from an incomplete or incorrect calculation.

 

• 30 (Option 3): This would result from calculating n(n−1) without dividing by 2, effectively double-counting each connection.

 

• 24 (Option 4): Not the correct value for a completely connected network of 6 nodes.

question: Which among the following is the largest of all the duns of the Shiwaliks mountain range in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dehra Dun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dehra Dun is the largest of all the duns (longitudinal valleys) of the Shiwalik range, situated between the Shiwalik Hills to the south and the Lesser Himalayas to the north. (देहरादून — शिवालिक का सबसे बड़ा दून)

 

• It stretches roughly 75–90 km in length and 15–20 km in width, and lies in the state of Uttarakhand.

 

• Duns are structural valleys formed by the folding of the Shiwalik ranges, and Dehra Dun is drained by rivers such as the Song and the Suswa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable duns include Kotli Dun, Patli Dun, and Kothri Dun, all much smaller than Dehra Dun.

 

• The city of Dehradun, the capital of Uttarakhand, takes its name from this dun valley.

 

NOTE

 

• Patli Dun (Option 1): A smaller dun valley in Uttarakhand, near the Yamuna river.

 

• Jammudun (Option 2): A relatively minor dun formation, much smaller than Dehra Dun.

 

• Kotli Dun (Option 4): Another smaller dun valley in Uttarakhand, located between the Ganga and Yamuna rivers.

question: Rajaraja I, considered the most powerful Chola ruler, became king in ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 985.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajaraja I (also known as Rajaraja Chola I), widely regarded as the most powerful ruler of the Chola dynasty, ascended the throne in 985 CE. (राजराज प्रथम — चोल वंश का सबसे शक्तिशाली शासक)

 

• He significantly expanded the Chola Empire, conquering parts of Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and the Malabar Coast, and built a strong navy.

 

• He commissioned the magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, completed around 1010 CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• His son, Rajendra Chola I, succeeded him and further extended the Chola Empire, including a celebrated naval expedition against the Srivijaya kingdom in Southeast Asia.

 

• The Cholas were noted for an advanced local self-government system, described in inscriptions such as those at Uttaramerur detailing village assemblies (sabhas).

 

NOTE

 

• 999 (Option 1): Not the correct year of Rajaraja I's accession.

 

• 979 (Option 2): Not the correct year; this predates his actual accession.

 

• 971 (Option 3): Not the correct year of his accession to the Chola throne.

question: The foundation of the Mauryan empire was laid by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE, after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty with the guidance of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya). (चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य — मौर्य साम्राज्य के संस्थापक)

 

• He established one of the largest empires of ancient India, extending from the Hindu Kush in the northwest to Bengal in the east.

 

• He later abdicated his throne, became a Jain monk under Acharya Bhadrabahu, and is believed to have died at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded by his son Bindusara, and later by his grandson Ashoka, the most celebrated Mauryan emperor.

 

• Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador at Chandragupta's court, wrote the famous account “Indica,” describing Mauryan society.

 

NOTE

 

• Kalashoka (Option 1): A ruler of the Shishunaga dynasty of Magadha, unrelated to the founding of the Mauryan Empire.

 

• Bindusara (Option 3): The second Mauryan emperor, son of Chandragupta Maurya, not the founder.

 

• Ashoka (Option 4): The third and most famous Mauryan emperor, grandson of Chandragupta, known for spreading Buddhism after the Kalinga war.

question:
Which of the following pair of "player – medal" is correct regarding performance of India in 2022 Commonwealth Games?
I. Bajrang Punia – Gold
II. Sakshi Malik – Gold
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Bajrang Punia won the Gold medal in men's freestyle wrestling (65 kg) at the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham.

 

• Statement II is correct: Sakshi Malik won the Gold medal in women's freestyle wrestling (62 kg) at the same Games — her first Commonwealth Games gold. (साक्षी मलिक — CWG 2022 स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• India's wrestling contingent had a highly successful campaign at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games, winning multiple gold medals across weight categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian wrestling gold medallists at CWG 2022 included Vinesh Phogat, Ravi Kumar Dahiya, Naveen Malik, and Deepak Punia.

 

• Sakshi Malik had earlier won a bronze medal in wrestling at the 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, as statement I (Bajrang Punia – Gold) is also true.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, as statement II (Sakshi Malik – Gold) is also true.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

question:
Sheela recalls using transistors as part of her computer.
Which generation of computers used it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Second-generation computers (approximately 1955–1965) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, making them smaller, faster, more reliable, and more energy-efficient. (द्वितीय पीढ़ी के कंप्यूटर — ट्रांजिस्टर)

 

• Transistors replaced the bulky, heat-generating vacuum tubes that had been used in first-generation computers.

 

• Examples of second-generation computers include the IBM 1401 and the IBM 7090.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Third-generation computers (1965–1971) used integrated circuits (ICs).

 

• Fourth-generation computers (1971–present) use microprocessors, while fifth-generation computers are built around artificial intelligence.

 

NOTE

 

• Third (Option 1): Used integrated circuits (ICs), not transistors.

 

• First (Option 2): Used vacuum tubes, as in machines like ENIAC and UNIVAC.

 

• Fourth (Option 3): Used microprocessors (large-scale integration), the basis of modern personal computers.

question: Madhubani style of painting originated in the state of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhubani painting (also called Mithila painting) originated in the Mithila region of Bihar, particularly around the Madhubani district. (मधुबनी चित्रकला — बिहार)

 

• It is traditionally created by women using natural dyes and pigments, applied with fingers, twigs, brushes, and matchsticks, on freshly plastered mud walls or on handmade paper and cloth.

 

• Common themes include Hindu deities (especially Krishna, Rama, and Durga), nature, and scenes from festivals and royal court life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhubani painting received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2007–08.

 

• The art form gained wider recognition in the 1960s, after a severe drought led local women to sell their traditional wall art as paintings on paper.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for art forms such as Pithora paintings and Rogan art, not Madhubani.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for Mysore paintings, not Madhubani.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Known for Phad paintings and Rajasthani/Mughal-style miniature paintings, not Madhubani.

question: Which singer was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Jewels) in the court of Mughal Emperor Jalal ud-din Mohammad Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tansen (born Ramtanu Pandey) was a legendary classical vocalist and instrumentalist who was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Jewels) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. (तानसेन — अकबर के नवरत्नों में से एक)

 

• He is credited with composing numerous ragas, including Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Todi, and Darbari Kanada, and is regarded as one of the greatest musicians in the history of Indian classical music.

 

• He originally served at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court around 1562.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other Navaratnas of Akbar's court included Birbal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Todar Mal, Raja Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Fakir Aziao-Din, and Mullah Do Piaza.

 

• A samadhi (memorial) dedicated to Tansen exists in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, where the annual Tansen Sangeet Samaroh music festival is held in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Alla Rakha (Option 1): A 20th-century tabla maestro, unrelated to Akbar's court.

 

• Ustad Ahmad Lahori (Option 2): The chief architect associated with the construction of the Taj Mahal under Shah Jahan, not a musician in Akbar's court.

 

• Amir Khusrau (Option 3): A celebrated poet-musician of the Delhi Sultanate era (13th–14th century), closely associated with Alauddin Khilji's court — he predates Akbar's reign by over two centuries.

question: Swachh Toycathon Competition 2022 was launched in India by Ministry of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swachh Toycathon Competition 2022 was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), inviting citizens to design innovative toys and games from waste/recycled materials around a “Swachhata” (cleanliness) theme. (आवासन और शहरी कार्य मंत्रालय — स्वच्छ टॉयकाथॉन)

 

• The competition aimed to promote cleanliness and waste-management awareness among children through creative, educational toys.

 

• It was launched as part of ongoing efforts under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• MoHUA also spearheads other major urban initiatives, such as the Swachh Survekshan rankings and the Smart Cities Mission.

 

• The broader “Toycathon 2021” national initiative, aimed at promoting India's indigenous toy industry, was a joint effort of multiple ministries.

 

NOTE

 

• Finance (Option 1): Not the ministry associated with this specific competition.

 

• Commerce and Industry (Option 2): This ministry was associated with the broader “Toycathon 2021” initiative on toy manufacturing, but the Swachh Toycathon 2022 specifically was launched by MoHUA.

 

• Culture (Option 4): Not the ministry responsible for launching this competition.

question: On which of the following dates does the summer solstice falls?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21 June.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs around 21 June each year, when the Sun appears directly overhead the Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N), giving the longest day and shortest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. (ग्रीष्म संक्रांति — 21 जून)

 

• On this date, the North Pole is tilted most directly toward the Sun due to Earth's axial tilt of approximately 23.5°.

 

• The corresponding winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs around 22 December, when the Sun is overhead the Tropic of Capricorn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equinoxes (equal day and night worldwide) occur around 21 March (spring/vernal equinox) and 23 September (autumnal equinox), when the Sun is directly overhead the Equator.

 

• In the Southern Hemisphere the seasons are reversed, so 21 June marks the winter solstice there.

 

NOTE

 

• 22 December (Option 1): The date of the winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere (summer solstice in the Southern Hemisphere).

 

• 23 September (Option 2): The date of the autumnal equinox, not the summer solstice.

 

• 21 March (Option 3): The date of the vernal (spring) equinox, not the summer solstice.
